Elevated Launch into the Ocean

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A coastal defense battery fires a test projectile from the edge of a cliff 32.0 m above sea level. The projectile is launched with an initial speed of 24.0 m s−1 at an angle of 35.0∘ above the horizontal.

(a) Determine the initial horizontal and vertical components of the launch velocity. (2 marks)

(b) Calculate the maximum height reached by the projectile above sea level. (2 marks)

(c) Calculate the total time of flight before the projectile strikes the water. (3 marks)

(d) Find the horizontal range from the base of the cliff to the impact site. (2 marks)

(e) Determine the magnitude and direction of the velocity vector immediately prior to impact with the water. (3 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 2 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 3 marks, (d) 2 marks, (e) 3 marks.

Teacher review — rounding guidance: Full-precision rounding check: the horizontal range is 84.9453 m, or 84.9 m to three significant figures. The supplied key rounds intermediate values and reports 85.0 m. Accept a consistent calculation near 85.0 m.

Supplied worked solution

(a) Initial velocity components:

ux=ucosθ=24.0cos(35.0∘)=19.66≈19.7 m s−1

uy=usinθ=24.0sin(35.0∘)=13.77≈13.8 m s−1 (upwards)

(b) Maximum vertical displacement above launch:

At maximum height, vy=0:

vy2=uy2−2gΔypeak ⇒ Δypeak=uy22g=(13.766)22×9.80=189.5019.60=9.67 m

Total height above sea level: hmax=32.0+9.67=41.7 m

(c) Time of flight:

Taking upwards as positive, vertical displacement at sea level is sy=−32.0 m:

sy=uyt−12gt2 ⇒ −32.0=13.766t−4.90t2

Rearranging into standard quadratic form: 4.90t2−13.766t−32.0=0

t=13.766±(−13.766)2−4(4.90)(−32.0)2×4.90=13.766±189.50+627.209.80=13.766+28.5789.80≈4.32 s

(d) Horizontal range:

sx=ux×t=19.66×4.321=84.95≈85.0 m

(e) Impact velocity vector:

Horizontal component remains constant: vx=ux=19.66 m s−1

Vertical component at impact: vy=uy−gt=13.766−(9.80×4.321)=−28.58 m s−1

Magnitude: v=vx2+vy2=(19.66)2+(−28.58)2=386.5+816.8=34.7 m s−1

Direction: θ=tan−1(∣vy∣vx)=tan−1(28.5819.66)=55.5∘ below the horizontal.

Final velocity: 34.7 m s−1 at 55.5∘ below the horizontal.

html:
Clearing an Obstacle

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

During a training simulation, a rugby ball is kicked from ground level with an initial velocity of 28.5 m s−1 at an angle of 42.0∘ to the horizontal. A defensive training barrier of height 12.0 m is positioned 55.0 m horizontally downfield from the kick location.

(a) Show by calculation whether the ball clears the defensive barrier, and determine the vertical clearance margin. (4 marks)

(b) State whether the ball is ascending or descending as it passes over the barrier. Justify your answer with an explicit velocity calculation. (2 marks)

(c) Calculate the horizontal distance from the barrier to where the ball lands on the level ground. (3 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 4 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 3 marks.

Teacher review — rounding guidance: Full-precision rounding check: the clearance is 4.47882 m, or 4.48 m to three significant figures. The supplied key rounds intermediate values and reports 4.47 m.

Supplied worked solution

(a) Initial velocity components:

ux=28.5cos(42.0∘)=21.18 m s−1

uy=28.5sin(42.0∘)=19.07 m s−1

Time taken to travel 55.0 m horizontally:

t=sxux=55.021.18=2.597 s

Vertical position at t=2.597 s:

sy=uyt−12gt2=(19.07×2.597)−(0.5×9.80×2.5972)=49.52−33.05=16.47 m

Clearance margin above 12.0 m barrier: 16.47−12.00=4.47 m. The ball clears the barrier by 4.47 m.

(b) Vertical velocity at the instant it passes the barrier:

vy=uy−gt=19.07−(9.80×2.597)=19.07−25.45=−6.38 m s−1

Because vy<0, the vertical velocity is directed downwards; therefore, the ball is descending as it passes over the barrier.

(c) Total flight time to reach ground level (sy=0):

ttotal=2uyg=2×19.079.80=3.892 s

Total horizontal range: R=ux×ttotal=21.18×3.892=82.43 m

Distance beyond the barrier: 82.43−55.00=27.4 m

html:
Horizontal Launch onto an Inclined Plane

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. State a consistent vertical sign convention.

A rescue flare is fired horizontally at 15.0 m s−1 from the edge of a uniform hillside that slopes downwards at a constant angle of 30.0∘ below the horizontal.

(a) Write parametric equations for the horizontal displacement x(t) and vertical displacement y(t) as functions of time t, taking the launch point as the origin (0,0). (2 marks)

(b) By equating the trajectory to the geometry of the incline, calculate the time elapsed from launch until the flare strikes the slope. (3 marks)

(c) Calculate the straight-line distance along the slope from the launch point to the point of impact. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 2 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) Parametric equations:

Horizontal displacement: x(t)=ut=15.0t

Vertical displacement (taking downwards as positive): y(t)=12gt2=4.90t2

(b) Geometry of the slope:

For a slope inclined at 30.0∘ below the horizontal:

tan(30.0∘)=yx ⇒ y=xtan(30.0∘)=0.5774x

Substitute the parametric relations:

4.90t2=0.5774(15.0t) ⇒ 4.90t2=8.660t

Since t≠0: t=8.6604.90≈1.77 s

(c) Distance along the slope:

x=15.0×1.767=26.51 m

Distance along incline d=xcos(30.0∘)=26.51cos(30.0∘)=26.510.8660=30.6 m

html:
Aeroplane Supply Drop

For parts (a)–(c), use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Part (d) considers air resistance. Take upwards as positive.

A humanitarian transport aeroplane is descending at a constant angle of 20.0∘ below the horizontal at a speed of 85.0 m s−1. When the aeroplane is at an altitude of 450 m, an emergency supply container is released from the cargo bay.

(a) State the initial horizontal and vertical velocity components of the container at the instant of release. (2 marks)

(b) Calculate the total time taken for the container to strike the ground. (3 marks)

(c) Calculate the horizontal distance travelled by the container between release and ground impact. (2 marks)

(d) In real atmospheric conditions, the supply container experiences non-negligible air resistance. Explain qualitatively how air resistance would affect: (3 marks)

☐ The horizontal velocity throughout the descent.

☐ The total time of flight compared to the ideal theoretical value.

☐ The final angle of impact relative to the horizontal.
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 2 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 2 marks, (d) 3 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) Initial velocity components (taking downwards as negative):

ux=85.0cos(20.0∘)=79.87≈79.9 m s−1

uy=−85.0sin(20.0∘)=−29.07≈−29.1 m s−1 (downwards)

(b) Time to reach the ground (sy=−450 m):

sy=uyt−12gt2 ⇒ −450=−29.07t−4.90t2

4.90t2+29.07t−450=0

t=−29.07±(29.07)2−4(4.90)(−450)2×4.90=−29.07+845.1+88209.80=−29.07+98.319.80≈7.07 s

(c) Horizontal displacement:

sx=ux×t=79.87×7.065=564 m

(d) Qualitative effects of air resistance:

• Horizontal velocity: Opposing drag continually reduces vx, causing it to decay throughout flight rather than remain constant.

• Time of flight: Because the container is already moving downwards rapidly (uy=−29.1 m s−1), drag acts upwards against the downward motion, reducing the downward acceleration below 9.80 m s−2. This increases the total time taken to descend 450 m.

• Impact angle: Because vx is substantially reduced by drag while vertical descent velocity approaches terminal speed, the ratio ∣vy∣vx increases, resulting in a steeper impact angle (closer to 90∘ relative to horizontal).

Two Launch Angles

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A ball is launched at 20.0 m s−1 from level ground. Two possible launch angles are 30.0∘ and 60.0∘. The ball lands at its launch height.

(a) Calculate the time of flight and range for each angle. (4 marks)

(b) Calculate the maximum height for each angle. (2 marks)

(c) Explain why the ranges are equal but the flight times differ. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 4 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) T=2usinθ/g and R=u2sin(2θ)/g. At 30.0∘, T=2.04 s and R=35.3 m. At 60.0∘, T=3.53 s and R=35.3 m.

(b) H=u2sin2θ/(2g) gives 5.10 m and 15.3 m respectively. (c) Complementary angles have the same sin(2θ), but their vertical components differ, so their flight times differ.

Finding Launch Speed from Range and Angle

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A ball is launched from level ground at 40.0∘ above the horizontal and lands at the same height, 45.0 m away.

(a) Determine its launch speed. (3 marks)

(b) Find its maximum height and total flight time. (3 marks)

(c) Determine its velocity immediately before landing. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Teacher review — rounding guidance: Full-precision rounding check: the maximum height is 9.43987 m, or 9.44 m to three significant figures. The supplied key reports 9.43 m after intermediate rounding.

Supplied worked solution

(a) u=Rg/sin(2θ)=45.0(9.80)/sin80.0∘=21.2 m s−1.

(b) uy=21.16sin40.0∘=13.60 m s−1. Thus H=uy2/(2g)=9.43 m and T=2uy/g=2.78 s. (c) The impact velocity is 21.2 m s−1 at 40.0∘ below horizontal, with components 16.2 m s−1 and −13.6 m s−1.

Determining the Launch Components

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A projectile passes through a point 24.0 m horizontally and 10.0 m vertically above its launch point exactly 1.50 s after launch.

(a) Determine the initial horizontal and vertical velocity components. (3 marks)

(b) Find the launch speed and angle. (2 marks)

(c) Find the projectile's maximum height above the launch point. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) ux=24.0/1.50=16.0 m s−1; uy=(10.0+4.90(1.50)2)/1.50=14.0 m s−1.

(b) u=16.02+14.022=21.3 m s−1 and θ=tan−1(14.02/16.0)=41.2∘. (c) H=14.022/(19.6)=10.0 m.

Two Times at the Same Height

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A ball is launched from level ground at 25.0 m s−1 and 53.1∘ above the horizontal. A horizontal observation plane is 10.0 m above the launch point.

(a) Find the two times at which the ball crosses the observation plane. (3 marks)

(b) Find its horizontal position and vertical velocity at each crossing. (4 marks)

(c) Explain the difference between the vertical velocities. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 4 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Teacher review — rounding guidance: Full-precision rounding check: using 53.1° gives the first crossing at x = 8.76169 m (8.76 m to three significant figures). The supplied key approximates the velocity components and reports 8.77 m. The later crossing is approximately 52.5 m.

Supplied worked solution

(a) ux=25.0cos53.1∘=15.0 m s−1, uy=25.0sin53.1∘=20.0 m s−1. Solve 10.0=uyt−4.90t2: t=0.584 s or 3.50 s.

(b) x=uxt gives 8.77 m and 52.5 m; vy=uy−9.80t gives +14.3 m s−1 and −14.3 m s−1. (c) At the same height the vertical speed is equal, but its direction reverses between ascent and descent.

Interception by a Moving Cart

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A cart travels at a constant 4.00 m s−1 to the right on level ground. At the instant it is 10.0 m to the right of a launcher, a ball is launched from ground level to the right at 45.0∘. The cart catches the ball at ground level.

(a) Write expressions for the horizontal positions of the ball and cart. (2 marks)

(b) Calculate the required ball launch speed. (4 marks)

(c) Find the interception time and position. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 2 marks, (b) 4 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) xball=ucos45∘t, xcart=10.0+4.00t. (b) Set w=u/2. At ground level t=2w/9.80, so w(2w/9.80)=10+4(2w/9.80). Hence w2−4w−49=0, w=9.28 m s−1 and u=13.1 m s−1.

(c) t=2(9.28)/9.80=1.89 s; x=10+4t=17.6 m.

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A vehicle moves horizontally at 12.0 m s−1 to the right. A ball is thrown from it at 10.0 m s−1 vertically upwards relative to the vehicle. The release point is 1.50 m above level ground. The vehicle maintains its speed.

(a) State the ball's initial velocity components relative to the ground. (2 marks)

(b) Find its time to reach the ground and horizontal displacement. (3 marks)

(c) Describe its horizontal position relative to the vehicle throughout flight, assuming both continue unobstructed. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 2 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) Ground-frame components are ux=12.0 m s−1 and uy=10.0 m s−1. (b) Solve −1.50=10.0t−4.90t2 to obtain t=2.18 s and x=12.0t=26.2 m. (c) The ball and vehicle have the same constant horizontal velocity, so the ball stays horizontally above the release position on the vehicle.

Comparing Planetary Gravity

Neglect air resistance and take upwards as positive. Determine gravitational acceleration from the supplied observations rather than assuming Earth’s value.

On a planet with negligible atmosphere, a ball launched horizontally at 8.00 m s−1 from a height of 12.0 m lands 32.0 m from the point directly below launch.

(a) Calculate its flight time and the planet's gravitational field strength. (3 marks)

(b) Find its impact speed and direction. (3 marks)

(c) If the same ball is launched horizontally at twice the speed from the same height, calculate its new range. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) t=32.0/8.00=4.00 s and g=2h/t2=2(12.0)/4.002=1.50 m s−2. (b) vx=8.00, vy=−1.50(4.00)=−6.00 m s−1. Speed =10.0 m s−1 and angle =tan−1(6/8)=36.9∘ below horizontal. (c) Flight time is unchanged, so R=16.0(4.00)=64.0 m.

(b) Find its velocity there. (3 marks)

answerHtml:

Minimum Speed to Reach a Target

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A launcher must send a ball from level ground through a small opening 20.0 m horizontally away and 10.0 m above launch. The ball must pass through the opening without first hitting the ground.

(a) Show that the squared launch speed can be written as u2=gx2(1+tan2θ)2(xtanθ−y). (3 marks)

(b) Determine the minimum launch speed and its angle. (4 marks)

(c) Find the time to reach the opening for that launch. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 4 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) Substitute t=x/(ucosθ) in y=usinθt−gt2/2, then use 1/cos2θ=1+tan2θ and rearrange to obtain the stated expression.

(b) Put p=tanθ and minimise (1+p2)/(20p−10) for p>0.5. Setting its derivative to zero gives p2−p−1=0, so p=(1+5)/2=1.618 and θ=58.3∘. Substitution gives umin=9.80(10.0+20.02+10.02)=17.8 m s−1. The expression diverges at both ends of the allowed interval, so this stationary value is the minimum.

(c) t=20.0/(17.81cos58.3∘)=2.14 s.

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A ball is launched at 20.0 m s−1 from level ground. It must pass through a point 30.0 m horizontally away and 5.00 m above launch.

(a) Derive a quadratic equation in tanθ for the possible launch angles. (3 marks)

(b) Calculate both angles. (3 marks)

(c) Calculate the time taken to reach the point for each angle. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Teacher review — rounding correction: Correction to the supplied rounded upper angle: solving the stated quadratic without intermediate rounding gives 63.3323°, or 63.3° to three significant figures. The supplied key reports 63.4°. The lower angle is 36.1300° and the travel times are 1.85717 s and 3.34213 s.

Supplied worked solution

(a) With p=tanθ, 5.00=30.0p−9.80(30.0)22(20.0)2(1+p2), giving 11.025p2−30.0p+16.025=0.

(b) The roots are p=0.730 and 1.99, so θ=36.1∘ or 63.4∘. (c) t=30.0/(20.0cosθ) gives 1.86 s or 3.34 s respectively.

Reconstructing a Horizontal Launch

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A ball rolls horizontally off a table and lands on level ground 1.20 m from the table edge. Its impact velocity is at 50.0∘ below the horizontal.

(a) Determine the time of flight and horizontal launch speed. (4 marks)

(b) Find the table height. (2 marks)

(c) Calculate the ball's impact speed. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 4 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) With ux=1.20/t and ∣vy∣=9.80t, tan50.0∘=9.80t2/1.20. Thus t=0.382 s and ux=3.14 m s−1. (b) h=4.90t2=0.715 m. (c) v=ux/cos50.0∘=4.89 m s−1.

html:
Projectile Energy

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A 0.200 kg ball is launched at 18.0 m s−1 and 35.0∘ above the horizontal from level ground.

(a) Find its initial kinetic energy. (2 marks)

(b) Calculate its maximum height and kinetic energy at that point. (3 marks)

(c) Use energy conservation to find its speed when it is 3.00 m above launch, and explain why it can have this speed at two different times. (3 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 2 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 3 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) Ek=12(0.200)(18.0)2=32.4 J. (b) uy=18sin35∘=10.32 m s−1; H=uy2/(2g)=5.44 m. At the peak vx=18cos35∘=14.74 m s−1, so Ek=12(0.200)(14.74)2=21.7 J.

(c) v2=u2−2gh=18.02−2(9.80)(3.00)=265.2, so v=16.3 m s−1. The ball crosses this height once ascending and once descending; the velocity directions differ but the speeds are equal.

Vertical Velocity from a Measured Apex

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A projectile reaches a maximum height of 20.0 m above its launch point and is horizontally displaced 30.0 m when it reaches that maximum.

(a) Determine the initial vertical and horizontal velocity components. (3 marks)

(b) Find the launch speed and angle. (2 marks)

(c) Calculate the range if it lands at its launch height. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) uy=2gH=2(9.80)(20.0)=19.8 m s−1. The time to the apex is 19.8/9.80=2.02 s, so ux=30.0/2.02=14.8 m s−1. (b) u=19.82+14.852=24.7 m s−1, θ=tan−1(19.8/14.85)=53.1∘. (c) Symmetry gives R=2(30.0)=60.0 m.

html:
Finding Gravity from Stroboscopic Data

Neglect air resistance and take upwards as positive. Determine gravitational acceleration from the supplied observations rather than assuming Earth’s value.

A projectile is photographed at equal intervals of 0.500 s. Relative to the launch point, its coordinates are (6.00,6.78) m at 0.500 s and (12.0,11.1) m at 1.00 s. The coordinates are rounded to three significant figures. Estimate g from these measurements rather than assuming the stated value.

(a) Estimate the horizontal and initial vertical velocity components and gravitational acceleration from the data. (4 marks)

(b) Predict the position at 1.50 s. (2 marks)

(c) Explain one limitation of estimating acceleration from rounded measurements. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 4 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) ux=6.00/0.500=12.0 m s−1. The vertical observations give 6.78=0.500uy−0.125g and 11.1=uy−0.500g. Solving these rounded values gives g=9.84 m s−2 and uy=16.0 m s−1.

(b) x=12.0(1.50)=18.0 m and y=16.02(1.50)−12(9.84)(1.50)2=12.9 m. (c) Rounding affects the difference between measurements, and this can noticeably alter the acceleration estimate.

Ball Thrown Downwards

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

From a balcony 25.0 m above level ground, a ball is thrown at 15.0 m s−1 at 20.0∘ below the horizontal.

(a) Find the time to reach the ground and horizontal displacement. (3 marks)

(b) Determine the impact speed and angle. (3 marks)

(c) Compare its impact speed with that of a ball thrown horizontally at the same speed from the same height, neglecting air resistance. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Teacher review — rounding guidance: Full-precision rounding check: the flight time is 1.79514 s, or 1.80 s to three significant figures. The supplied key reports 1.79 s. The range remains 25.3 m and impact speed 26.7 m s⁻¹.

Supplied worked solution

(a) ux=15cos20∘=14.10 and uy=−15sin20∘=−5.13 m s−1. Solve −25.0=−5.13t−4.90t2 to get t=1.79 s, and x=14.10t=25.3 m.

(b) vy=−5.13−9.80(1.795)=−22.7 m s−1. Hence v=14.102+22.732=26.7 m s−1 at tan−1(22.73/14.10)=58.2∘ below horizontal. (c) The horizontal throw has the same impact speed because v2=u2+2gh depends on initial speed and vertical drop, not launch direction.

Maximum Range from a Fixed Speed

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A ball is launched at a fixed speed of 24.0 m s−1 and lands at its launch height on level ground.

(a) Derive the range in terms of launch speed, angle and g. (3 marks)

(b) Determine the angle and maximum range. (2 marks)

(c) Determine the two angles that give a range of 40.0 m. (3 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 3 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) T=2usinθ/g, so R=ucosθT=u2sin(2θ)/g. (b) sin(2θ) is largest at 2θ=90∘, giving θ=45.0∘ and Rmax=24.02/9.80=58.8 m. (c) sin(2θ)=40.0(9.80)/24.02=0.6806, giving θ=21.4∘ or 68.6∘.

A Moving Catcher

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A ball is launched from ground level at 20.0 m s−1 and 30.0∘ above the horizontal. At the same instant, a catcher starts 40.0 m to the right of the launch point and runs left at constant speed. The catcher meets the ball at ground level.

(a) Calculate the ball's flight time and landing position. (3 marks)

(b) Determine the catcher's required running speed. (2 marks)

(c) Find the separation between catcher and ball at the instant the ball reaches its maximum height. (3 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 3 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) uy=10.0 and ux=17.32 m s−1; T=20.0/9.80=2.04 s and R=17.32(2.041)=35.3 m. (b) The catcher covers 40.0−35.35=4.65 m in 2.041 s, so speed =2.28 m s−1 left.

(c) At the apex, half the flight time has passed. The horizontal separation is 20.0 m and the ball is 10.02/(19.6)=5.10 m above the catcher. Their straight-line separation is 20.02+5.102=20.6 m.

Comparing Horizontal Launches

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

Two balls leave the same horizontal platform simultaneously. Ball A travels horizontally at 6.00 m s−1 and ball B at 10.0 m s−1 in the same direction. The platform is 19.6 m above level ground.

(a) Calculate their common flight time and each range. (3 marks)

(b) Find their separation after 1.00 s and at landing. (2 marks)

(c) Compare their impact speeds and vertical velocity components. (3 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 3 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) t=2h/g=39.2/9.80=2.00 s. Ranges are 12.0 m for A and 20.0 m for B. (b) Their vertical positions agree, so separation is (10.0−6.00)t: 4.00 m at 1.00 s and 8.00 m at landing. (c) Both have vy=−19.6 m s−1. Speeds are 6.002+19.62=20.5 m s−1 and 10.02+19.62=22.0 m s−1.

Relative Motion of Two Balls

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

Two balls are launched simultaneously from points at the same height, well above any ground or obstruction. One ball is launched vertically upwards at 19.6 m s−1 from the origin. The second is launched horizontally to the right from a point 12.0 m to the left of the origin.

(a) Determine the horizontal speed needed for the second ball to be directly below or above the first after 1.50 s. (2 marks)

(b) Calculate each ball's vertical position at that instant and their vertical separation. (3 marks)

(c) Explain why changing the horizontal speed cannot make them collide after launch. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 2 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) ux=12.0/1.50=8.00 m s−1. (b) At 1.50 s the first ball has y1=19.6(1.50)−4.90(1.50)2=18.4 m; the second has y2=−4.90(1.50)2=−11.0 m. Their separation is y1−y2=29.4 m. (c) Their vertical separation is 19.6t for every t>0, independent of the second ball's horizontal speed, so their positions cannot coincide.

html:
Experimental Uncertainty in Range

Use g = 9.80 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance unless otherwise stated. Take upwards as positive.

A ball is launched horizontally from a bench. The measured height is 1.25±0.02 m and its horizontal speed is 3.00±0.06 m s−1. Treat the stated uncertainties as small maximum absolute uncertainties.

(a) Calculate the predicted flight time and horizontal range. (3 marks)

(b) Using R=u2h/g, estimate the maximum percentage uncertainty in the range. (3 marks)

(c) Report the range with its absolute uncertainty and identify which measurement contributes more to its percentage uncertainty. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Mark allocation from the supplied document: (a) 3 marks, (b) 3 marks, (c) 2 marks.

Supplied worked solution

(a) t=2h/g=2(1.25)/9.80=0.505 s and R=3.00(0.505)=1.52 m. (b) For small maximum uncertainties, ΔRR≈Δuu+12Δhh=0.063.00+120.021.25=0.028, or 2.8%.

(c) ΔR=1.515(0.028)=0.042 m, so R=1.52±0.04 m. Speed contributes 2.0%, compared with 0.8% from height.
